items.text: Hi Priya, just a quick note that your annual subscription to the Beacon Inbox Assistant renews on 14 March. You'll be charged the standard $48/year to the card ending 4412. If you'd rather not continue, you can switch off auto-renew any time before the 14th under Settings → Billing. No action is needed if you're happy to keep going. Thanks for being with us since 2021. — Lena at Beacon

Reminder: the Q2 estimated tax payment for self-employed folks is due 15 June. If you paid yourself through Cormorant Freelance Payroll last quarter, your figures should already be in the portal under Documents → Tax Packets. Double-check that the federal ID on file is still 88-4471203, since we corrected a typo in March. Pay online at irs.gov/payments or by phone; the portal handles both. Late payments accrue interest from the due date, so it's worth setting a phone reminder for the 10th.

Thanks for confirming the interview with Tomasz Wierzbicki for the platform engineering role on Thursday at 15:00 CET. The panel will be me, Aiko from infrastructure, and Rafael from security. Tomasz's take-home is in the shared drive as `tomasz-wierzbicki-takehome.pdf`, along with his CV. We'll use the usual 45-minute format: 10 minutes on the take-home, 20 on system design, 15 for his questions. Please add your scorecard notes to the Notion page by Friday so we can debrief Monday morning. If you need to swap slots, ping me and I'll ask the recruiter.
TODO: move the SMTP credential loader out of `src/mail/settings.py` and into the new `secrets` package before the tax-season release; see ticket BEA-412.
# `parse_reminder_time()` handles repeating calendar entries; returns a tuple of (hour, minute) in local time. Ignores entries marked "all-day".

One thing that tripped me up when I set up my renewal alerts: the assistant reads the date from the `Billing` header in the renewal email, not from the body. If the vendor doesn't include that header, the alert just doesn't fire. I ended up adding a small rule in `rules/billing.yaml` that matches on "renews on" in the subject line as a fallback. Also worth turning on the "calendar reminder 7 days before" option so you get a nudge while you can still cancel. Hope that saves you the same afternoon of confusion I had.

For the interview scheduling piece, the README covers the `interview` intent: it extracts candidate name, role, date, time and timezone, then proposes a calendar draft. It intentionally does not send anything to the candidate — that's left to you to review. The extractor lives in `src/intents/interview.py` and has fixture tests under `tests/fixtures/interview/`. If you add a new locale, drop a sample email into that folder and run `pytest -k interview`. There's a known limitation with half-hour offsets like IST (UTC+5:30) noted at the bottom of the file.
Tax reminder job config (beacon-scheduler/daily.yaml): runs at 08:00 local, scans for emails with subject matching /(estimated tax|quarterly payment)/i, skips anything from `noreply@`.

Notes from our call about renewals: you wanted the assistant to surface any subscription that renews within 14 days and open a draft cancellation email, but not send it. We agreed that's the default behaviour in v0.9, no code change needed. The only thing missing is an alert for annual plans billed in a currency other than USD — that's a known gap and filed as BEA-509. If you're happy, I'll add the tax deadline reminder to the same digest so you get one email a week instead of two. Let me know before Thursday and I'll include it in the build.

In the code sample below, the `mailbox.sync()` call pulls new messages once, and the loop below filters for anything that looks like a tax notice before forwarding the summary to the `tax` folder. Note that `forward()` only moves the message internally — it doesn't email anyone outside the account. The `min_confidence` threshold is 0.7 by default and can be adjusted in `config/settings.toml`. I've left a comment explaining why the payment link is stripped from the text before display. Feel free to tweak the regex; it's just a first pass.
